subject: physics
question_text: Which of the following physical quantities has no dimensions: angular velocity, angular acceleration, angular displacement, stress?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The answer
lines: θ = arc / radius = s / r, a length divided
by a length, so both units cancel.
steps.why: Any ratio of two quantities of the same kind is dimensionless. The radian is a name for that ratio, not a unit with dimensions of its own.
common_mistakes: Thinking that because the radian is a unit, angular displacement must have dimensions. The radian is a unit, but a dimensionless one: [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰]. Having a unit does not mean having dimensions.

recall.must_convey: That angular displacement is dimensionless because it is arc divided by radius.

steps.memory_tip: A ratio of two lengths cancels. The radian is a name, not a dimension.
steps.margin_note: Write s/r. It is the proof in three characters.

steps.label: Why not the others
lines: Each of these carries at least one dimension,
so angular displacement is the only one left.
steps.why: Angular velocity is a dimensionless angle divided by time, so it keeps the T⁻¹ from the time alone — which is why it is not dimensionless.
common_mistakes: Writing ω as dimensionless because θ is. Dividing by time adds T⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That angular velocity is one over time, angular acceleration one over time squared, and stress is M L to the minus one T to the minus two.
accept: M L minus one T minus two

steps.memory_tip: θ is dimensionless, but θ/t is not — the time brings T⁻¹ with it.
steps.margin_note: One line rules out all three.

insider_note: Asked in AP March 2026. The answer is angular displacement — a ratio of two lengths, so the units cancel.
